papers.title: A long-term organotypic slice culture model of patient high-grade glioma preserving tumor heterogeneity and architecture, and specificity of CAR T cell targeting
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: High grade glioma (HGG), encompassing IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (CNS WHO grade 4), diffuse midline glioma (CNS WHO grade 4), oligodendroglioma (IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted) CNS WHO grade 3, together with IDH-mutant astrocytoma of CNS grade 3 and grade 4, represents the most lethal group of adult diffuse gliomas. Despite significant efforts, obtaining improvements in patient survival has been limited, in part, by difficulties in comprehensive ex vivo modeling of the complexities of HGG. Although organotypic slice cultures and other platforms have shown promise, existing models often fail to capture the intrinsic cellular heterogeneity, microenvironment, and architecture of HGG, restricting investigations into their fundamental biology as well as design of novel therapeutics. Methods: We developed a patient-derived HGG organotypic slice culture (GOSC) platform demonstrating long-term preservation of intrinsic tumor characteristics. Vibratome-sectioned slices were cultured in defined medium under conditions approximating those in situ: reduced oxygen (4%), low glucose (2.5 mM), and no added growth factors. The characteristics of GOSCs after 28 days in culture, including expression of immunotherapy targets, were compared to parental tumors using histological staining, immunofluorescence, multiplexed PhenoCycler (CODEX) imaging, bulk RNA-seq expression profiling, and CAR T cell killing assays. Results: GOSCs preserved the histopathology, cell heterogeneity, tumor microenvironment, and tissue architecture of their parental tumors throughout at least 28 days in culture. Importantly, GOSCs retained parental patterns of immunotherapy target expression, and CAR T cells co-cultured with GOSCs demonstrated target-specific killing consistent with parental tumors. Conclusions: This ex vivo GOSC platform offers long-term preservation of the cellular and structural properties of parental HGG tumors, thereby providing a robust tool for extended preclinical studies, and facilitating development and evaluation of advanced tumor-targeting strategies.

papers.title: Genomic classification and immune profiling define mucosal melanoma
papers.abstract: Mucosal melanoma is a rare, lethal melanoma subtype with distinct genetics and limited benefit from immunotherapy. To define features associated with mucosal melanoma clinical outcomes, we assembled a large, multimodally profiled cohort spanning primary and metastatic disease. Compared with cutaneous melanoma, primary mucosal melanoma showed greater genomic heterogeneity, ploidy and aneuploidy, and a more dedifferentiated, proliferative transcriptional state. Analysis of genomic sequencing of 339 patients with mucosal melanoma identified four mutually exclusive genomic subtypes: CDK4/MDM2/CCND1, SF3B1-mutated, TP53/ATRX, and mucosal melanoma Triple WT, associated with distinct anatomic sites but similar outcomes. In the tumor microenvironment, we observed reduced T cell infiltration and increased CD163+ tumor-associated macrophages in mucosal melanoma relative to cutaneous melanoma. In matched longitudinal samples, CD163+ tumor-associated macrophages increased with disease progression and immunotherapy resistance. CD163+ tumor-associated macrophages engaged non-regulatory T cells through GAL9-TIM-3 interactions, nominating TIM-3 blockade as a therapeutic strategy for mucosal melanoma. These findings define the distinct aggressive biology of mucosal melanoma and highlight potential therapeutic targets and mechanisms of immune resistance.

papers.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF Inhibitor
papers.abstract: Therapeutic inhibition of the RAS/MAPK cascade, an oncogenic driver in over one-third of human cancers, has been limited by a core trade-off: effective pathway blockade in tumors versus dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors successfully mitigated this trade-off in BRAF-monomer-driven tumors, an equivalent strategy has been lacking for RAF-dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations. Here, we characterize ELV-3111, a next-generation, potent, and selective Type 1 RAF inhibitor that overcomes this limitation via a distinct mechanism of action. ELV-3111 induces paradoxical MAPK hyperactivation in normal tissues by binding RAF and promoting the active conformation (priming) followed by rapid dissociation (fast off-rate), a biochemical feature that spares RAS-mutant tumors, where RAF is already primed. In these and other RAF dimer-driven tumor models, ELV-3111 achieves potent and selective MAPK and growth suppression. When combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 enables complementary pharmacology: additive inhibition in tumors and compensatory effects in normal tissues. The combination produced durable regressions across RAS-mutant and BRAF-mutant models, including a RAS-mutant model refractory to current therapies, while maintaining favorable tolerability. Thus, we uncover a generalizable mechanism that enables Type 1 RAF inhibitor plus MEK inhibitor combinations to achieve tumor-selective MAPK suppression, with the potential to inform targeted therapy design.

papers.title: DDR and TMEM132 genes control progenitor targeting and regenerative assembly of the planarian eye
papers.abstract: How progenitors can faithfully self-assemble to build new organs in adulthood is a central unsolved problem in regeneration biology. The planarian eye is a model for uncovering principles of de novo organogenesis during regeneration. In this process, pluripotent adult stem cells specify into ovo+ migratory progenitors which target to the eye field due to Wnt and FGFRL signals produced from bodywall muscle, then differentiate into photoreceptor neurons (PRNs) and pigmented optic cup (OC) cells, followed by organization of these two cell types in an opposing pattern that completes eye organ maturation. We used scRNA-seq to characterize eye progenitor transcriptomes during regeneration, followed by FISH validation, and RNAi screening to identify regulators of eye regeneration. This uncovered a function for the discoidin domain receptor ddr-1 in preventing the premature terminal differentiation of migratory eye progenitors. DDRs encode collagen receptors, and bodywall muscle is the major source of collagen in planarians, suggesting eye progenitors likely interface with muscle ECM for their proper deployment in regeneration. We further identified a novel eye morphogenesis phenotype from knockdown of tmem132-1, causing failed heterotypic adhesion between eye cell types. TMEM132 factors are conserved cell-surface receptors that mediate adhesion and regulate migration, and human TMEM132 mutations are associated with several neurobehavioral diseases. Therefore, planarian tmem132-1 likely directly regulates the capture and assembly of migratory progenitors into mature eyes during regeneration. Together, these results define new steps in the eye regeneration pathway and suggest ancient roles for DDR and TMEM132 in progenitor migration and coordinated organ assembly.

papers.title: Spatially restricted bmp16 in an extra-embryonic syncytium promotes dorsoventral patterning
papers.abstract: How nuclei within a shared cytoplasm organize gene expression programs to direct developmental signaling remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic mapping, and functional perturbations to characterize the zebrafish yolk syncytial layer (YSL), an extra-embryonic syncytium that supports embryonic development and patterning. We identify extensive transcriptional covariation among YSL nuclei, revealing coordinated multigene programs organized along dorsoventral and animal-vegetal axes. Within the YSL, we identify an animal-ventral subdomain expressing several BMP ligand transcripts including bmp16, a member of the BMP2/4 subfamily. We found bmp16 expression to be exclusively extra-embryonic during gastrulation, and functional perturbations reveal that bmp16 is sufficient to ventralize embryos upon overexpression and acts synergistically with bmp2b to promote ventral fates. Ventral YSL expression of Bmp transcripts depends on a transcriptional program downstream of mxtx2 and is maintained independently of BMP pathway autoregulation, while negative regulation by hhex restricts bmp16 expression to the ventral YSL. Together, these findings establish the YSL as a spatially organized syncytium in which coordinated nuclear gene expression programs support localized sources of embryonic patterning signals.

papers.title: Peroxisome quality control is gated by a dynamic ATF6α-ABCD3 tether
papers.abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) coordinates protein folding and lipid biosynthesis, while peroxisomes govern fatty-acid catabolism and redox balance. However, little is known about the mechanisms by which these organelles communicate. Here we show that activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), a cytoprotective ER-resident sensor of the unfolded protein response (UPR), forms a molecular tether that zippers the ER and peroxisomes together at a 23-nm intermembrane distance. ATF6 achieves this by inserting a short segment of its unstructured N-terminal cytosolic tail into the solvated transmembrane cavity of the peroxisomal ABC-type lipid transporter ABCD3, trapping it in an off-state. This interaction is reinforced by Ceapin, a previously identified small molecule molecular-glue ligand, which promotes ER-peroxisome contact formation. The junctions serve as a scaffold that can initiate peroxisome turnover by p62-triggered autophagy (pexophagy), as enhanced lipid processing resulting from organelle zippering leads to peroxisome damage due to excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. These findings define ATF6 as a non-transcriptional regulator of organelle quality control and provide a template for engineering Ceapin analogues against ATF6/ABCD3-dependent colorectal and hepatocellular cancers and related diseases.

papers.title: Conserved Fibroblast Subsets Drive Shared Fibrotic Mechanisms in Osteoarthritis Synovium and Systemic Sclerosis Skin
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) and systemic sclerosis (SSc) are diseases with distinct etiologies but similar disease phenotypes, most prominently fibrosis, a process governed by the pathological activation of fibroblasts. Mechanisms underpinning fibrosis in these diseases are widely studied, though have yet to be directly compared. We employed single-cell RNA-seq and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics to describe the functional plasticity and the range of fibroblast activation states in both diseases. We identified disease-enriched fibroblast subsets conserved in both diseases, including fibrogenic myofibroblast-like cells, chemokine- and cytokine-expressing inflammatory fibroblasts, and lining-like fibroblasts. These subsets exhibited convergent fibrotic programs also observed in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, as well as overlapping osteochondral transcriptional programs. Xenium 5K spatial transcriptomics revealed that conserved, disease-associated fibroblasts reside in highly similar anatomic niches in OA synovium and SSc skin. These consisted of a fibrotic ECM-rich niche harboring myofibroblast-like cells and an inflammatory niche containing inflammatory fibroblasts adjacent to infiltrating immune cells. Disease-associated transcriptional remodeling converged on shared functional pathways and common putative upstream molecular regulators. These findings identify conserved cellular states, spatial niches, and regulatory programs across OA and SSc, suggesting that fibrotic disease is underpinned by shared pathogenic stromal states and candidate targets for therapeutic strategies are applicable across both diseases.

papers.title: Protein-level mapping reveals novel Immune State Types (ISTs) associated with Chlamydia trachomatis infection, inflammatory remodeling, and scarring in trachoma-hyperendemic Amhara Ethiopia
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Trachoma remains the leading infectious cause of blindness. Over 100M people are at risk, and 1.9M already live with visual impairment or blindness. Ethiopia bears the greatest burden of disease with ~61M or 59% of the known affected global population. Although Chlamydia trachomatis (Ct) infection initiates disease, infection alone fails to explain why inflammation resolves in some but progresses to irreversible scarring and vision loss in others. Previous studies have largely examined gene expression or limited protein panels, leaving the conjunctival immune protein environment poorly characterized. We hypothesized that distinct conjunctival immune states capture these pathogenic processes and could reveal biomarkers for selecting treatment and surveillance strategies. Methods and Findings: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 667 participants residing in the hyperendemic Amhara region of Ethiopia at least one year after the most recent azithromycin mass drug administration to treat Ct. The upper tarsal conjunctivae was graded for TF and TI, trachomatous inflammation-follicular or intense, respectively; I-TS/TT, inflammation with scarring with or without trichiasis, defined as one or more eyelashes touching the globe of the eye; and TS and TT, scarring with or without trichiasis but no inflammation. T0 represented no trachoma. The protein concentrations of 41 immune mediators were quantified using Meso Scale Discovery electrochemiluminescence immunoassays. Associations with infection and grade were evaluated using covariate-adjusted models with false discovery rate correction. Bernoulli mixture modeling (BMM) revealed four distinct Immune State Types (ISTs). Both approaches supported a shared biological framework characterized by selective immune activation in Ct infection, broad inflammation in TF/TI, and chemokine remodeling versus immune quiescence in the scarred conjunctiva. Ct infection was associated with a focused IFN-{gamma}-centered response. IST1 captured this immune response where 51.9% of the participants had Ct; we therefore termed IST1 Quiescent Infection. In contrast, TF/TI was associated with higher concentrations of proinflammatory, Th1/Th17, chemokine, regulatory, and remodeling pathways mediators. This profile fit well within IST2, termed Broad Inflammation, where 72.4% of the participants had TF/TI. TS/TT retained considerable chemokine activity, whereas I-TS/TT showed a narrower, IL-17A-dominant inflammatory profile. BMM separated scarring into two states characterized by distinct profiles: IST3, Conjunctival Remodeling, with significantly stronger chemokine and T-cell maintenance signals; and IST4, Quiescent Scarring, with the majority of chemokines being significantly downregulated. This suggests that scarred conjunctiva can retain substantial immune activity or shift toward a more attenuated state. Conclusions: This study establishes the first IST framework for trachoma, revealing biologically distinct immune states with different potential clinical implications. IST1 indicates the need for antibiotic treatment, whereas IST2 suggests that novel immunotherapeutics might be effective in thwarting disease progression. The upregulated chemokines in IST3 may indicate risk of progression to TT necessitating prospective studies and potential novel antifibrotic interventions. Together, our findings provide a strong biological foundation for stratifying patients by immune state and matching them to preventive and therapeutic care. Prospective validation and streamlined biomarker panels will support the translation of this framework into field settings to help avert disease progression and blindness.

papers.title: KRAS-driven metabolic reprogramming of enhanced MFSD2A-mediated lysophosphatidylcholine scavenging promotes survival and progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Oncogenic KRAS drives lipid reprogramming in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) to promote disease progression, and these changes are manifest in circulation. Using mass spectrometry, we performed lipidomic analyses on plasmas from a cohort of 93 newly-diagnosed resectable PDAC cases, 43 patients with chronic pancreatitis, and 93 age- and sex-matched healthy controls, the results of which revealed pronounced reductions in circulating lysophosphatidylcholines (LysoPC) as a prominent feature associated with PDAC. Using stable-isotope resolved lipidomics, we further found that PDAC cells exhibit a lipid scavenging phenotype characterized by preferential uptake of extracellular unsaturated LysoPCs to sustain pro-growth signals. Restricting bioavailability of extracellular unsaturated LysoPCs shifted the metabolic phenotype of PDAC cells towards enhanced de novo lipogenesis and autophagy, which was accompanied by suppression of AKT signaling activities and increased susceptibility to apoptosis. Using bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets together with functional experiments, we identified oncogenic KRAS-mediated upregulation of major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 2a (MFSD2A) as a key mediator that facilitates extracellular uptake of LysoPCs in PDAC cells. Loss of MFSD2A expression mimicked LysoPC restriction and resulted in inhibition of AKT signaling and increased propensity of PDAC cells to undergo apoptosis in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Therapeutic targeting of the KRAS-MFSD2A-LysoPC axis via repurposing of the synthetic alkyl-lysophospholipid edelfosine promoted potent anti-cancer effects in vitro that were mechanistically attributed to reduced extracellular uptake of LysoPCs, and attenuation of AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings describe a previously unrecognized onco-metabolic program of enhanced LysoPC scavenging mediated by MFSD2A that promotes PDAC progression and that is therapeutically targetable via repurposing edelfosine.

papers.title: In situ identification of pre-hematopoietic stem cells and their niche
papers.abstract: Definitive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) emerge predominantly along the ventral surface of the dorsal aorta in the embryonic aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM) region, yet the spatial organization of the niche underlying this developmental asymmetry remains poorly understood. Defining the native niche of pre-HSCs has also been hindered by their rarity, transient nature and lack of a single definitive marker for their identification in situ. Here, we integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to construct a spatiotemporal atlas of the niche in the AGM. Neural cells and chondrogenic mesenchyme predominated dorsally, whereas N-cadherin mesenchymal stromal cells (N-cad+ MSCs) formed a ventral layer between the aortic endothelium and mesonephric cells. BMP and SHH signaling showed overall dorsal enrichment, whereas WNT, NOTCH and KIT signaling were enriched ventrally, with these cellular and signaling patterns dynamically remodeled across HSC ontogeny. Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics validated the findings and further enabled the identification of individual pre-HSCs in situ and revealed a multicellular niche comprising endothelial cells, N-cad+ MSCs, intra-aortic hematopoietic cluster cells and macrophages. TGF{beta} and NOTCH signals were primarily supplied locally, whereas major sources of BMP and WNT were more distant. Functional perturbation identified niche-derived CD200 as an immune-regulatory signal promoting HSC development, validating a spatially predicted niche interaction. Together, our findings link tissue-scale spatial organization with the local multicellular niche supporting the preferential development of HSCs along the ventral aorta.

papers.title: WNT/β-catenin increases 3D chromatin mobility and reorganisation during posterior cell state transitions
papers.abstract: Chromatin mobility, the exploration of 3D conformations by the chromatin fibre, is implicated in transcription and DNA repair, and is thought to decrease progressively as cells differentiate. Here, combining live-cell 3D single-nucleosome tracking with genomic approaches, we show that chromatin mobility instead changes in a cell-type-specific manner, increasing as pluripotent cells acquire posterior fates. This is accompanied by 3D genome reorganisation, including loss of Polycomb-associated interactions and emergence of CDX2-associated interactions. Withdrawal of posteriorising WNT/{beta}-catenin signalling rapidly reduces chromatin mobility and partially restores Polycomb-associated chromatin interactions, while Cdx1/2/4-null cells fail to acquire these WNT/{beta}-catenin-dependent changes. Together, our findings establish chromatin mobility as a regulated property of cell state, with WNT/{beta}-catenin signalling and CDX factors acting as mediators that fine-tune the sampling of 3D chromatin interactions during cell state transitions.

papers.title: The annexin A1 mimetic peptide Ac2-26 promotes inflammation-resolution and stimulates skeletal muscle regeneration in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disorder mainly affecting young boys characterized by repeated cycles of myofiber injury/regeneration and chronic muscle inflammation. Although glucocorticoids can slow disease progression, their potential long-term adverse effects highlight the need for new steroid-sparing therapies for DMD. Annexin A1 (ANXA1) is a glucocorticoid-induced pro-resolving protein that signals primarily through formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2). We investigated whether the ANXA1 mimetic peptide Ac2-26 could reduce inflammation, stimulate tissue regeneration, and improve skeletal muscle function in muscular dystrophy. 3-week-old dystrophin-deficient male mdx mice were randomized to receive daily intraperitoneal injections of vehicle control, deflazacort (1 mg/kg/day), or Ac2-26 (1 mg/kg/day) for a duration of 5-weeks. Body composition, skeletal muscle mass, contractile function, and tissue histopathology/immune-cell infiltration were assessed at 8-weeks of age. Direct effects on myogenesis were also examined in vitro using primary D2-mdx myoblasts. ANXA1 was expressed predominantly by myeloid cells rather than resident dystrophic muscle cells. Both deflazacort and Ac2-26 markedly reduced intramuscular inflammation and increased myofiber size. However, Ac2-26 produced broader anabolic and functional benefits, increasing body-weight gain, lean body mass, hindlimb muscle weights, and absolute contractile force. Ac2-26 treatment also directly promoted myogenesis of dystrophic myoblasts in vitro, while pharmacological FPR2 blockade impaired myotube development. Overall, Ac2-26 mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of deflazacort while providing superior benefits for body weight and composition, skeletal muscle growth, myofiber regeneration, and absolute muscle strength. These findings support therapeutic targeting of the ANXA1-FPR2 axis as a potential safe and effective steroid-sparing immunomodulatory strategy for DMD.

papers.title: A decision-based criterion and a resolution threshold for ranking genomic prediction models within trials
papers.abstract: Breeding programmes choose genomic prediction models by accuracy rankings, and the metric behind a ranking decides which model wins. Selecting the best genotypes within a trial depends only on the order of the predictions, so a metric that guides the choice must be unchanged by any order-preserving change of the predictions and respond when their order is reversed. Of the 22 official metrics of the Genomes to Fields maize competition, one meets both conditions, the within-environment rank correlation; the within-environment Pearson correlation is protected against rescaling only; and twenty fail, including the root mean squared error that decided the 2022 ranking. Switching between the competitions two official metrics reverses 27 % of team pairs, and an exact decomposition shows why pooled metrics mislead: in three constructed panels, 94-95 % of the attainable square of pooled correlation is carried by the environment means. The accuracy difference a trial can resolve falls as about 3/{surd}N with its N genotype-environment cells: at least 0.03 at the competitions design and 0.04-0.12 once calibrated on real panels, against 0.003 between the first two teams; tests that two correlations differ declare far smaller differences, which do not reliably change selection. In soybean, where the two most accurate methods stand clear of most others by more than the trial resolves, ranking by either within-environment correlation selects better material, 98-99 % of the attainable selection gain in held-out environments against 13-34 % for error-magnitude rankings; in common bean and a Chinese maize population, where the leading methods lie within the resolvable gap, all rules pick material of similar value. GPverdict runs these checks on any programmes cross-validated predictions.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of PtaAGL16 improves post-drought recovery and shoot vitality in hybrid poplar
papers.abstract: Drought stress severely limits tree growth and survival, a problem intensifying under climate change due to the rising frequency of extreme weather events. Identifying genetic variants that modulate drought stress responses and enhance resilience is therefore of great interest for developing climate-adapted trees. While the MADS-box transcription factor AGL16 has been implicated in drought responses and stomatal regulation in herbaceous species, the function of its homolog in woody perennials remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the role of PtaAGL16 in the poplar hybrid Populus tremula x P. alba. We generated CRISPR/Cas9 knockout lines of PtaAGL16 in the poplar clone INRA 717-1B4. Plants were subjected to a severe drought stress regime followed by a re-watering recovery phase. Morphological and physiological traits, including growth, stomatal conductance, shoot vitality, and stomatal density, together with stress-associated metabolites and drought-responsive gene expression, were analyzed. All agl16 knockout lines exhibited significantly reduced drought-induced damage compared to the wild-type. While the wild-type suffered extensive defoliation and persistent stem necrosis, the knockout lines retained higher shoot vitality and resumed growth after re-watering, including the formation of new leaves. Consequently, vitality in the knockout lines reached up to 86%, compared to only 34% in the wild-type. This improved resilience was accompanied by reduced persistent oxidative membrane damage, as indicated by lower MDA levels after recovery. These findings indicate that the disruption of PtaAGL16 is associated with enhanced drought resilience in a woody perennial species and highlight its potential as a genetic target for improving climate adaptation in fast-growing forest trees.

papers.title: Radiotherapy-induced vascular dysfunction alters neutrophil phenotype to promote tumor cell colonization of mammary adipose tissue
papers.abstract: Recurrence remains a significant clinical challenge for triple-negative breast cancer patients and radiotherapy (RT) is a key therapeutic tool that significantly reduces the risk of relapse. Despite this, patients with chronic lymphopenia and a high neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio (NLR) experience recurrence at significantly higher rates than those whose hematological biomarkers return to baseline post-RT, and there are currently no treatments to prevent this relapse. Here, we utilized in vivo mouse models of lymphocyte-deficiency to identify the mechanism behind systemic immune status and recurrence. Using a model of RT-induced circulating tumor cell (CTC) colonization, we found that neutrophils are sustained in the irradiated, lymphocyte-deficient mammary tissue up to 10 days post-RT. Persistent neutrophil accumulation was accompanied by excessive vascular remodeling and tumor cell colonization of the mammary tissue, both of which were abated upon systemic neutrophil depletion. Neutrophils in the colonization-permissive microenvironment exhibited a state of pathological activation consistent with a polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cell (PMN-MDSC) phenotype that was not seen in systemic compartments, highlighting a microenvironment-induced phenotype shift. This phenotype was recapitulated in vitro when naive neutrophils were exposed to the secretome of RT-induced senescent endothelial cells (ECs). We found that these activated neutrophils then regulated the dysfunction of irradiated ECs in a canonical NF-kB-dependent manner, increasing their barrier permeability and activating downstream inflammatory signals. Our findings not only establish neutrophils as a critical component of tumor cell colonization in lymphocyte-deficient subjects but also uncover a positive feedback loop between neutrophils and irradiated vasculature that leads to aberrant tissue remodeling and ultimately tumor cell colonization. This work deepens our understanding of how systemic factors influence treatment-damaged microenvironments, which could ultimately lead to identification of molecular targets for prevention of RT failure.

papers.title: EPHA4 Regulates the Transition between Mesenchymal and Hybrid States in TNBC
papers.abstract: Metastatic progression in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is strongly influenced by epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), which enables transitions between epithelial, hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal (E/M), and mesenchymal cell states. While mesenchymal cells are highly invasive and resistant to therapy, hybrid E/M states confer advantages during metastatic colonization. Both mesenchymal and hybrid states therefore contribute to tumor aggressiveness through distinct mechanisms. However, the molecular regulation governing transitions between mesenchymal and hybrid E/M states remains poorly understood. Here, we identify EPHA4 as a regulator of this transition in TNBC. EPHA4 expression is enriched in mesenchymal TNBC cells, and genetic knockout of EPHA4 in MDA-MB-231 xenograft and 4T1 syngeneic models induces a shift toward hybrid E/M phenotypes. This transition reduces cellular invasion while enhancing metastatic colonization, consistent with the clinical observations of decreased EPHA4 expression in secondary metastases compared to primary tumors. Despite compensatory changes in other Eph/ephrin family members following EPHA4 loss, EPHA4 deficiency is sufficient to drive this phenotypic shift. These findings identify EPHA4 as a regulator of cancer cell plasticity in TNBC and highlight the therapeutic complexity of targeting pathways that govern metastatic state transitions.

papers.title: A tonic PDGFA-dependent niche organizer maintains alveolar homeostasis
papers.abstract: Tissue homeostasis requires mechanisms that preserve quiescence while allowing rapid activation after injury, but how tissues actively restrain injury responses during homeostasis remains poorly understood. Here we identify alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells as organizers of the distal lung niche through tonic expression of PDGFA, which maintains alveolar fibroblast identity and restrains myofibroblast activation. Cell type-specific ablation revealed that loss of AT1s, but not other major alveolar cell populations, was sufficient to evoke spontaneous fibroblast activation and tissue-wide responses that recapitulate injury. In silico ligand-receptor analysis, ex vivo screening, and conditional genetic models identified AT1-derived PDGFA as a key homeostatic signal. Loss of AT1-derived PDGFA caused spontaneous myofibroblast induction and tissue remodeling, whereas increasing PDGFA promoted fibroblast proliferation while suppressing myofibroblast differentiation. Integrated phosphoproteomic, transcriptomic, and chromatin accessibility analyses showed that PDGFA engages SHP2-ERK signaling, suppresses MRTFA-associated SRF programs, and promotes E2F-associated cell-cycle programs, thereby opposing the pro-fibrotic effects of TGF{beta}-driven fibroblast activation. Restoring PDGFA signaling abrogates myofibroblast features from human idiopathic pulmonary fibrotic lungs and attenuated fibrotic remodeling in vivo. These findings define a tonic AT1-derived PDGFA signal that maintains alveolar homeostasis and offers a therapeutic target to prevent or revert lung fibrosis.

papers.title: Glutathione Protects Hematopoietic Stem Cells from Proteotoxic Stress
papers.abstract: Glutathione is a redox buffer, best known for preventing oxidative stress and ferroptosis, but rarely studied in stem cells. We studied glutathione function in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) by deleting the glutamate-cysteine ligase catalytic subunit (GCLC), which synthesizes glutathione, or glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), which employs glutathione to prevent ferroptosis. GCLC deficiency eliminated glutathione from hematopoietic cells, severely impairing HSC function and hematopoiesis. In contrast, GPX4 deficiency did not affect HSC function and had little effect on hematopoiesis, even after vitamin E depletion, suggesting glutathione has ferroptosis-independent functions in HSCs. Consistent with this, GCLC deficiency increased reactive oxygen species levels in hematopoietic cells. But treatment with antioxidants or ferroptosis inhibitors gave little or no rescue of HSC function despite reducing ROS levels. Rather, GCLC-deficient, but not GPX4-deficient, HSCs exhibited unfolded protein accumulation, proteostatic stress, and cell death marked by elevated p53 levels and Annexin V staining. Deficiency for p53 prolonged the function of GCLC-deficient HSCs after transplantation. Glutathione is thus necessary in HSCs for proteostasis but may be dispensable for ferroptosis inhibition in vivo.

papers.title: Metabolic commitment to human motor neurons is characterized by mitochondrial depletion and pyruvate rewiring
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial remodelling is a key feature of neurogenesis in cortical and hippocampal neuronal lineages, yet the temporal control of organellar homeostasis in developing human motor neurons remains poorly understood. Here, we generated a high-resolution temporal resource integrating proteomics, metabolomics, and mitochondrial characterization across human iPSC-to-motor neuron differentiation. This analysis revealed prolonged mitochondrial depletion during early neurogenesis, characterized by reduced mitochondrial content, mitochondrial fragmentation, and lysosome-dependent turnover. This state persisted throughout the neural progenitor stage and was followed by recovery of mitochondrial content during neuronal maturation. During this transition, pyruvate utilization shifted from pyruvate carboxylation towards pyruvate dehydrogenase-dependent oxidation. Pharmacological manipulation of pyruvate partitioning demonstrated that this metabolic switch is required for human neuronal differentiation. Our findings establish a temporal framework for the metabolic control of human motor neuron differentiation and reveal a progenitor-specific state linking mitochondrial depletion to pyruvate metabolism.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases (PepRePs), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/threonine phosphatase subunit to localize phosphatase activity to a target protein. We first establish the PepReP architecture using characterized tau-binding peptides, then apply protein language model-guided peptide design to target Rab8A, PTEN, and STAT3. Across endogenous and exogenous targets, PepRePs reduce phosphorylation, with downstream effects on tau aggregation, Rab8A-associated protein interactions, and cellular proliferation following PTEN and STAT3 targeting. Sequence-based peptide design enables targeting without structural inputs, supporting application to substrates with disordered regions that challenge conventional structure-based binder design. By coupling programmable peptide binders with modular phosphatase subunits, PepRePs enable targeted control of protein phosphorylation to probe cellular signaling and develop strategies for correcting disease-associated protein dysfunction.

papers.title: Targeted tumor desialylation by engineered probiotic reprograms the tumor microenvironment to potentiate immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Tumor hypersialylation drives immunosuppression and limits immunotherapy efficacy by shielding tumor cells and engaging inhibitory immune receptors. Here, we engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN{Delta}pgi-SAS) as a metabolically confined "desialylation catalyst" to remodel the tumor microenvironment. This strain combines HER2-directed adhesion, hypoxia-inducible surface sialidase display for targeted glycan cleavage, and sialic acid catabolism to prevent glycolytic recycling. Critically, disrupting glucose metabolism ({Delta}pgi) restricts bacterial proliferation to sialic acid-rich tumor microenvironment, significantly enhancing biosafety. In mice, EcN{Delta}pgi-SAS colonized tumors and effectively desialylated tumor cells, synergizing with anti-PD-L1 to suppress growth of immunologically "cold" tumors. Mechanistically, desialylation reversed immunosuppression by broadly enhancing antitumor immunity. Orally administered EcN{Delta}pgi-SAS substantially inhibited colorectal carcinogenesis, repaired epithelial barrier integrity by restoring tight junctions, and prevented adenoma formation. This integrated strategy establishes a clinically translatable platform for reversing immunosuppression in solid tumors.

papers.title: Studying the role of climate and sex in flowering dynamics of black poplar across time and space
papers.abstract: Global change has a major impact on rivers and their associated terrestrial compartment, the riparian forest. The black poplar (Populus nigra L.), the dominant species of the European riparian forest, is considered an indicator of the biodiversity dynamics of these ecosystems, but is threatened with extinction in several parts of its range. The species is dioecious and shows wide variability in many traits, enabling it to adapt to a broad range of environmental conditions. A detailed characterization of this natural variability is therefore a key issue both for the conservation of natural populations and for biological engineering aimed at restoring riverbanks. Phenology is both an indicator of climate change and an adaptation lever for populations, particularly in perennial species such as trees. In this study, we characterized the spatial and temporal variability in flowering phenology by studying 13 natural black poplar populations along the Loire River, France. Flowering date and duration showed substantial variability both within and between populations, and males generally flowered earlier than females. Despite this variability, the ranking of individual trees' flowering dates was highly consistent across years. Most male-female pairs shared several days of overlapping flowering each year, and this overlap was moderately stable across years. Flowering dates advanced by about five to six days per degree Celsius during early spring, with no detectable difference in sensitivity between sexes. This work contributes to the characterization of flowering variability in an economically important tree species and may inform both the conservation of genetic resources and breeding.

papers.title: Myosin-Driven Nuclear Movement Generates Stromules in Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.abstract: Plastids form stroma-filled tubular extensions, termed stromules, that are implicated in inter-organellar communication. In pathogen-challenged Nicotiana benthamiana, stromule formation is driven by kinesins acting along microtubules. However, whether this mechanism also operates in unstressed plants or in other species remains unknown. Using systematic genetic analysis of all class XI myosin genes and quantitative time-lapse imaging in Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana), we show that basal stromule formation is predominantly myosin dependent through two distinct mechanisms. Myosin XI-I generates most stromules by driving oscillatory nuclear movement that mechanically pulls stromules from stationary plastids within the approx. 8m wide stromule-promoting zone. Myosins XI-K, XI-1, and XI-2 additionally drive a movement-independent, nucleus-associated stromule subpopulation within the same zone, establishing two mechanistically distinct pathways. We propose that movement-coupled stromules function as dynamic tethers maintaining plastid-nucleus proximity during nuclear oscillations, while movement-independent stromules expand the plastid membrane area within the perinuclear space, increasing the potential contact surface with the nucleus and surrounding environment. Together, both populations are proposed to enhance signal and metabolite exchange at the plastid-nucleus interface. These findings indicate that stromule biogenesis is both mechanistically and functionally context dependent, challenging the universality of the kinesin-microtubule model across plant species and physiological states.

papers.title: Epidemic potential of Maravalia cryptostegiae, a classical biological control agent of rubber vine, in Northeastern Brazil
papers.abstract: Rubber vines (Cryptostegia madagascariensis and C. grandiflora) are highly invasive weeds in the semi-arid landscapes of many tropical regions. The rust fungus Maravalia cryptostegiae has provided a spetatular and sustainable control of invasive C. grandiflora populations in Australia, after its scientific and quarantine-authorized release in the context of a classical biological control program. The Caatinga biome of Northeastern Brazil is under a devastating invasion by C. madagascariensis. This species is also susceptible to M. cryptostegia but its epidemic potential towards C. madagascariensis in Brazil remains unknown. We developed a weather-driven epidemiological model integrating experimentally derived relationships for infection as a function of temperature and wetness duration and temperature-dependent latent development. Three infection-response models were fitted to 20 experimental temperature x wetness combinations found in the literature and evaluated using information criteria and grouped cross-validation. The selected model incorporated wetness-dependent thermal breadth and provided the best overall fit (R2 = 0.931), with prolonged wetness significantly broadening the thermal range favorable for infection. The infection and latent-development models were coupled with 25 years (2001-2025) of hourly meteorological data from 65 grid cells representing rubber-vine-infested locations in Northeastern Brazil. May-July accounted for >60% of annual infection potential, with the highest epidemic potential in Central Ceara and Western Paraiba, overlapping major host-infestation areas. Cross-continental evaluation at 13 historical monitoring sites in Queensland, Australia, reproduced documented wet-season epidemic patterns and differentiated high-impact coastal/riparian from drier inland environments. These results demonstrate strong seasonal and geographic structuring of epidemic potential, providing a quantitative basis for identifying locations and periods favorable for M. cryptostegiae establishment and epidemic development following its future release in Brazil.

papers.title: Dynamic 2'-O-Me of rRNA regulates ribosome translation in Arabidopsis nucleolin1 mutants and during seed-to-seedling transition
papers.abstract: Across all kingdoms of life, 2'-O-ribose methylation (2'-O-Me) is the most abundant modification of ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs), which are central to ribosome assembly and function. The 2'-O-Me of specific rRNA sites is catalysed by C/D-box small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein (snoRNP) complexes. However, how and when the landscape of plant rRNA 2'-O-Me modifications is remodelled remains largely unexplored. To study the regulation of rRNA 2'-O-Me and its impact on ribosome translation, we characterised Arabidopsis NUCLEOLIN 1 (NUC1)-depleted plants, which exhibit reduced 2'-O-Me at dozens specific rRNA sites, and investigated the impact of 2'-O-Me in ribosome translation during plant development. We demonstrated that 2'-O-Me is dynamically regulated during seed-to-seedling transition. Our analysis identified differentially methylated rRNA sites, which are specifically located in structurally critical regions of the ribosome. Notably, this hypomethylation is uncoupled from the global expression, assembly, or subcellular localisation of C/D-box snoRNPs. We further observed that polysomes with low 2'-O-Me levels not only accumulate but also exhibit differential mRNA loading. These polysomes characterised by reduced 2'-O-Me at specific rRNA sites, influence multiples aspects of translation, including ribosomes stalling at the initiation, elongation and termination steps. Together, these findings advance our understanding of the dynamic regulation of rRNA 2'-O-methylation and its functional role in ribosome-mediated translation in plants.

papers.title: HMGA2 Expression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Controls Tumor Microenvironment and Immunosuppression via IL1α
papers.abstract: The basal-like subtype of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is associated with poor outcomes and increased chemoresistance. Expression of high mobility group AT-hook 2 (HMGA2), a chromatin architectural protein, marks basal PDAC cells and associates with specific features of the tumor microenvironment (TME), including more immunosuppressive cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and fewer cytotoxic CD8+ T cells. Expression of HMGA2 by tumor cells leads to upregulation of the immunosuppressive markers interleukin 6 (IL6) and leucine-rich repeat containing protein 15 (LRRC15) in associated fibroblasts. Mechanistically, HMGA2 in the tumor cell binds the interleukin 1 alpha (IL1) promoter and upregulates transcription, increasing IL1 in the TME, in turn inducing immunosuppressive fibroblast polarization, increasing regulatory T cells, and decreasing CD8+ T cells. Blockade of the IL1 signaling axis disrupts this tumor-driven microenvironment phenotype and combines with inhibitors of oncogenic KRAS to improve tumor control.

papers.title: RNA and protein are not interchangeable in single-cell spatial multi-omics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics is increasingly used to infer cellular phenotypes, molecular interactions, and functional tissue organization from RNA, although most of these biological processes are ultimately mediated by proteins. Here, we directly tested the interchangeability of spatial RNA and protein measurements using paired Xenium profiling of 21 matched targets across ~1.8 million cells from primary lung adenocarcinoma and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. After accounting for marker- and dataset-specific protein background, we quantified concordance at multiple levels, including single-cell detection, expression magnitude, cell-type distribution, patient-level abundance, and spatial organization. Agreement at single-cell level was strongly marker-dependent. Canonical lineage markers generally showed concordant RNA and protein patterns, whereas several molecules, including in our study PD-1, PD-L1, and LAG-3, showed little concordance across modalities. Importantly, spatial organization remained substantially more discordant between modalities than overall abundance, indicating that spatial biomarkers are not directly transferable across modalities. Together, our results show that spatial RNA and protein measurements provide largely overlapping information for lineage markers and overall abundance, but can diverse for specific molecules and for higher-order spatial features, where the two layers provide complementary rather than equivalent readouts. These findings provide practical guidance on when spatial transcriptomic readouts can be interpreted as proxies for protein and when orthogonal protein validation is advisable.

papers.title: Integrin α3β1 is required for alveolar-capillary barrier formation through regulation of epithelial differentiation
papers.abstract: Laminin-binding integrins regulate critical morphogenic processes, but their specific roles in lung development are unknown. In this study, we combined an in vivo model of epithelial 3 subunit deletion in the murine lung with a multiomics approach to investigate the role of the epithelial 3{beta}1 integrin during murine lung development. We demonstrate that 3{beta}1 integrin is dispensable for airway branching morphogenesis due to delayed epithelial expression. Instead, in vivo deletion of 3{beta}1 integrin impaired alveolar epithelial cell differentiation and disrupted alveolar-capillary barrier formation, functionally limiting gas exchange. A discontinuous alveolar BM contained abnormal collagen IV and laminin networks and widened the gap between epithelial and endothelial cells in the alveolar-capillary barrier niche. Mechanistically, mice deficient in epithelial 3{beta}1 integrin possessed an intracellular trafficking and secretion defect for BM components. Thus, integrin 3{beta}1 orchestrates the temporal maturation of alveolar epithelial cells required for organization of the alveolar-capillary barrier.

papers.title: Adenosine refines the balance of spermatogonial proliferation and differentiation
papers.abstract: The balance between spermatogonial proliferation and differentiation is essential for sustaining male fertility, yet the contribution of cellular metabolism remains poorly understood. Here, we showed that adenosine levels increased significantly during spermatogonial differentiation and promoted the formation of differentiating spermatogonia. Using a conditional knockout mouse model in which Ahcy, a gene encoding an enzyme in adenosine synthesis, is deleted from spermatogonia, we found that disruption of adenosine generation blocked spermatogonial differentiation, resulting in a transient delay in spermatogenesis. We further demonstrated that adenosine exerted its effects partially through ADORA2A- and ADORA2B-mediated signaling. Downregulating these receptor activities by specific inhibitors in spermatogonial culture or by genetic ablation in mice led to increased spermatogonial proliferation. Taken together, our study identified adenosine as a metabolic signal in refining the balance between spermatogonial proliferation and differentiation, linking cellular metabolism to critical developmental timing and stem cell fate decisions.

papers.title: TriPort tangential flow filtration: a lab-assembled system for EV isolation across diverse cell-culture sources
papers.abstract: Tangential flow filtration (TFF) is an effective method for scalable EV isolation. Here, we describe and validate a reference protocol for TriPort-TFF, a laboratory-assembled TFF system featuring a three- port reservoir design enabling sample circulation, retentate return, and diafiltration. Constructed from individually sourced, commercially available components with detailed assembly and operating parameters, TriPort-TFF can be built at a lower cost than commercially integrated TFF platforms. We evaluated the system using conditioned media (CM) from human MDM cultured with EV-depleted human serum, human cerebral organoids in serum-free medium, and mouse BMDM cultured with EV-depleted foetal bovine serum (FBS) unstimulated or LPS-stimulated. The system reproducibly isolated EVs from all three sources, and biological replicates of BMDM showed distinct proteomic clusters between LPS-stimulated and unstimulated conditions. The requirement for subsequent size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) after TFF depended on the sample serum-presence. In serum-containing CM, TFF alone co-concentrated serum proteins alongside EVs, subsequent SEC improved the particle-to- protein ratio, reduced inter-replicate variability and improved proteomic depth. TFF alone in serum- free organoid CM already yielded higher particle-to-protein ratios than TFF-only preparations from serum-containing CM, with SEC further improving this ratio. TriPort-TFF offers an accessible system for EV-isolation that can be combined with SEC for diverse sample types.
